Expectation1: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation1: A friend sends a text message complaining about having a long, boring day.
Situation2: They coordinate closely with contractors to keep the construction schedule on track.
Story: My phone buzzed just as I was reviewing the latest site updates. It was Mia, my closest friend, texting, “Ugh, today was endless. Can I vent?” I glanced at the clock—contractors were waiting for my call to finalize tomorrow’s work. As an architect, I knew every minute counted; delays meant missed deadlines and angry clients. But Mia’s messages kept coming, each one heavier than the last. I could almost hear her voice, needing me to listen, to be present, to care. My mind raced: if I ignored her, I’d be a terrible friend, but if I paused my work, the project could slip off track. My heart tugged in two directions—toward the friend who needed comfort, and the team relying on my leadership. I stared at my phone, torn, feeling the weight of both worlds pressing in, unsure which to answer first.
